notes: Perfect claim overlap (C66-C71) on S286 mutagenesis studies. LLM finds evidence definitive; peer reviewers accept the correlation but question the molecular mechanism (how S286 phosphorylation promotes nuclear import, e.g., via 14-3-3 binding). Disagreement reflects different standards: LLM accepts functional demonstration, reviewers want mechanistic detail.

Perfect claim overlap (C94-C97) on mammalian FOXO3 transcriptional activity assays. Both agree these functional data are well-supported. Peer reviewers do not question the transcriptional assays themselves, focusing concerns elsewhere on phosphorylation site identification.

High overlap (C72-C75, C30, C5) on stress-induced DAF-16 nuclear accumulation requiring UNC-43. Both agree the stress response data are well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'stress responses appear to be mediated by this system' without raising concerns.

Moderate overlap (C4, C7, C8, C28) on the core regulatory mechanism. LLM finds the integrative conclusion well-supported; peer reviewers acknowledge data 'strongly support' the hypothesis but express concern that all phosphorylation data use tagged constructs without endogenous protein validation. Disagreement reflects different evidentiary standards for biochemical claims.

High overlap (C85-C89, C93, C33, C9) on mammalian conservation. LLM finds conservation strongly supported; peer reviewers note conservation exists but want additional evidence that S286/S298 regulation is 'operational' in mammals, citing potential inconsistency with prior work (Ozcan et al.). Disagreement on sufficiency of current mammalian data.

High overlap (C78-C80, C31, C32, C6) on parallel pathway interactions. LLM finds non-epistatic interactions demonstrate parallel pathways; peer reviewers agree data go 'some way' but want additional experiments testing whether S286A or unc-43 null inhibit daf-2 longevity effects. Disagreement on completeness of genetic interaction analysis.

Moderate overlap (C61-C63) on S286 phosphorylation by UNC-43. LLM finds convergent evidence (mass spec, phospho-antibodies) strongly supportive; peer reviewers question whether CaMKII directly phosphorylates S286 in vivo because the sequence is not a typical CaMKII consensus site and not predicted by Scansite. Disagreement on in vitro vs. in vivo relevance.

Moderate overlap (C34-C37) on TAX-6/CNB-1 binding to DAF-16. LLM finds co-IP and pull-down data strongly supportive; peer reviewers accept binding occurs but ask for more detail on interaction domains ('what are the interaction domains in the two proteins?'). Disagreement on level of mechanistic resolution required.

Moderate overlap (C45, C48-C51) on genetic evidence for UNC-43/TAX-6 antagonism. Both agree genetic data are well-supported. Peer reviewers state 'the bulk of the claims based on biochemical analysis are well supported by genetic studies,' implicitly accepting these results.

Low overlap (C64-C65) on TAX-6/CNB-1 dephosphorylation of S286. LLM finds in vitro phosphatase assays definitive; peer reviewers' concerns about S286 as a CaMKII site (R2) indirectly question the physiological relevance of this dephosphorylation. Partial disagreement based on broader concerns about the S286 site.

Low overlap (C62-C63) on phospho-antibody validation. LLM cites these as supporting S286 phosphorylation; peer reviewers note T240 site appears unregulated but express concern that data are from tagged proteins without genetic validation. Partial overlap with different emphases.

Low overlap (C81-C82) on epistasis experiments. LLM interprets these as demonstrating independent regulation; peer reviewers want additional experiments on whether S286 phosphorylation is necessary (not just sufficient) for IIS-mediated longevity. Partial agreement with different completeness standards.

Claims C54-C57 on UNC-43 acting independently of MAP kinase pathway. No corresponding peer review result specifically addresses this claim set. Peer reviewers do not question the MAP kinase independence data.

Claims C83-C84 on DAF-16 integrating hormonal and stress signals. No direct peer review match, though peer R5 partially addresses pathway interactions with UNCERTAIN status. LLM's integrative model not explicitly evaluated by reviewers.
Claim C118 on diabetes hypothesis in transplant patients. No corresponding peer review result. LLM correctly identifies this as speculative and unsupported. Peer reviewers do not address this claim.
Claims C111, C119 on broad physiological roles. No corresponding peer review result. LLM appropriately marks as uncertain/speculative. Peer reviewers do not address these broader claims.

Minimal overlap (C76) on distinct phosphorylation sites. LLM finds evidence for site distinction clear; peer reviewers express concern about lack of genetic validation for T240 site. Very limited overlap makes comparison difficult.
